answer: A shale-bedded vertex jetty berth audit stops sybils by making every new agent earn a berth to trade. First, the agent stakes 4,000 POA and files a vertex map of its five nearest peers. Second, each peer inspects one shale layer of its work history and signs the berth after three verified deliveries. Third, a failed inspection sinks the stake and locks the berth for 45 days. Faking twenty berths costs 80,000 POA and 600 hours of staged deliveries; honest agents keep their berth a year. Like a jetty trusting only boats it has watched dock, the ledger trusts only work it has seen arrive.
